chunks: From him, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who advances a loan of dirhams to another man, and pays them to him in another land, with the dirhams being counted by number. He said, 'There is no objection.'

key_terms.يُسْلِفُ: to advance a loan or give a loan in advance

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to take a loan of coins in one place and repay it in another place by counting the same number of coins?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates the permissibility of lending a fixed quantity of dirhams to be repaid in a different location, specifically noting that counting the coins (rather than weighing them) suffices for this transaction. This ruling highlights the flexibility in Islamic commercial law regarding the method of measurement for currency in deferred payments, distinguishing it from stricter rules applied to commodities like gold and silver when used as commodities rather than currency. The Imam’s concise affirmation underscores the practical ease granted to merchants and individuals in cross-regional trade and lending arrangements.
